specName: Convention Pack System + Agent Persona Pipeline
title: rorca-convention-agents
_notes: Convention packs (greenfield scaffolding), convention inference (brownfield extraction), convention drift detection, agent persona system (15+ personas in 4 categories), adversarial review pipeline, multi-pass spec generation (6-pass), MCP HTTP transport migration (API-first, auto-generated MCP from OpenAPI), and skills integration (LLM-driven skill matching, SkillRegistry, skills.sh CLI bridge, skill injection in execution engine). Depends on rorca-context-intent-engine for .rorca/ directory, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, and virtual context routing infrastructure.
_relatesTo: rorca-context-intent-engine (direct dependency — CIE provides .rorca/ infrastructure this spec builds on), rorca-opencode-integration (extends OC-019 complexity scorer with persona assignment), rorca-execution-quality (extends EQ-001 objective gates with adversarial review), rorca-v2-platform V2-102-V2-105 (extends direction stack wizard with convention inference)
_executionOrder: After rorca-context-intent-engine (spec #3), before rorca-e2e-testing (spec #4). CIE creates .rorca/ directory, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, routing engine. This spec layers convention packs + personas + skills on top. E2E testing should run last to test the complete system including conventions, personas, and skills.

userStories.title: Convention Pack Schema and Registry
userStories.description: Define the canonical pack.json schema (name, version, compatibility, dependencies, description) and a local pack registry in .rorca/packs/. Create a PackRegistry class that can list installed packs, resolve pack paths, and validate pack.json against a Zod schema. Store pack metadata in a new `convention_packs` SQLite table (id, workspace_id, pack_name, pack_version, installed_at, pack_path).
acceptanceCriteria: pack.json Zod schema validates: name, version, description, compatibility (node, frameworks), dependencies (other packs)
PackRegistry class: listInstalled(), getPackPath(name), validatePack(path) -> ValidationResult
convention_packs table created via pragma table_info pattern (not migration file)
Registry reads from .rorca/packs/ directory and cross-references DB for metadata
Invalid pack.json throws ValidationError with specific field-level errors
pack.json schema includes optional `skills` field (array of skill names bundled with the pack)

userStories.description: Implement PackLoader that reads the canonical pack directory structure: pack.json, direction/ (L1-engineering.md, L2-domain.md), personas/, conventions/, templates/, scaffold/, AGENTS.md. Each subdirectory has a defined contract. The loader returns a typed Pack object with all content resolved. Handle missing optional directories gracefully (personas/ and conventions/ are optional, direction/ and scaffold/ are required).

conventions/ files are plain markdown (library-specific guides)
scaffold/ is a directory tree that gets copied verbatim to the project root

userStories.title: Convention Inference Agent — Brownfield Context Extraction
userStories.description: Build a convention inference agent that analyzes an existing codebase and generates convention artifacts. Uses OpenCode (if available) or claude --print to: read package.json + config files to identify stack, scan file structure to infer architecture, read existing CLAUDE.md/README to extract conventions, analyze code patterns to generate observations. Produces: Direction Stack L3 content, CLAUDE.md (if missing), AGENTS.md with inferred file governance, and a conventions/ directory with per-library guides. Results are staged for human review (not auto-applied). Expose as POST /api/conventions/discover with { workspaceId }.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/conventions/discover spawns an analysis agent against workspace.path

Produces structured output: { stack, architecture, conventions, fileGovernance, directionL3 }
Results stored in a new convention_proposals table (workspace_id, proposal_json, status: pending|approved|rejected, created_at)
Results are NOT auto-applied — stored as a proposal for human review
Frontend can display proposal via GET /api/conventions/proposals/:workspaceId

userStories.title: Convention Drift Detection
userStories.description: Build a drift detector that compares current code against declared conventions in .rorca/conventions/ and direction stack. Runs an analysis agent that reads convention files and samples the codebase for violations. Returns a drift report with specific file:line references. Can be triggered manually (POST /api/conventions/check) or automatically as a pre-execution pipeline hook (checked before pipeline trigger if enabled in .rorca/config.json). Drift report stored in wal_events.

userStories.title: Adversarial Review Pipeline — Post-Story Review Passes
userStories.description: After each story implementation pass succeeds (exit 0), run review passes with the story's reviewers[] personas. Each reviewer gets the git diff of the story's changes + the reviewer persona prompt, and produces a structured review (issues[], suggestions[], blockers[]). If any reviewer flags a blocker, the story is marked as needing revision (not auto-passed). Review results stored in story_comments table. This is an opt-in feature controlled by .rorca/config.json adversarialReview: true.
acceptanceCriteria: After story passes (exit 0), execution-engine checks story.reviewers[] array
If reviewers exist and config.adversarialReview is true, runs N review passes sequentially

userStories.title: Multi-Pass Spec Generation — PM and Spec Writer Passes (Passes 1-2)
userStories.description: Refactor POST /api/specs/generate to support multi-pass mode. Pass 1 (PM Agent): takes the brief and generates a high-level spec with coarse user stories (10-20). Pass 2 (Spec Writer Agent): takes the coarse spec and decomposes each story into micro-stories with exhaustive acceptance criteria. Each pass creates a spec version in spec_versions table. Multi-pass is opt-in: a 'multiPass' boolean in the generate request body. When disabled, existing single-pass behavior is preserved.

userStories.title: MCP Streamable HTTP Transport — API-First Auto-Generated MCP
userStories.description: Migrate from hand-written stdio MCP tools to auto-generated MCP over HTTP. The Express API's OpenAPI spec at /api/docs/openapi.json becomes the single source of truth for all MCP tools. Use openapi-mcp-generator or equivalent to generate MCP tool definitions from the OpenAPI spec at startup. Serve MCP via Streamable HTTP transport on the same :3030 port at /mcp path. All existing and new API routes (including convention pack, persona, drift detection endpoints) become MCP tools automatically with zero hand-written MCP code. Keep the existing stdio MCP server as an offline fallback but mark it as legacy.

userStories.title: Skills.sh CLI Integration + Echolocation Bridge
userStories.description: Add skills.sh integration to the skills API routes. POST /api/skills/install-from-sh — runs `npx skills add <name>`, copies result to .rorca/skills/. GET /api/skills/suggestions — runs workspace echolocation, maps detected stack to skill names via existing STACK_TO_SKILLS mapping and inferredSkills field in workspace-echolocation.ts. POST /api/skills/search — proxy to skills.sh search API for marketplace browse. Wire up echolocation's inferredSkills output to SkillRegistry suggestions.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/skills/install-from-sh runs npx skills add <name> and copies result to .rorca/skills/
GET /api/skills/suggestions uses workspace echolocation to suggest skills based on detected stack
POST /api/skills/search proxies to skills.sh search API for marketplace browsing
Echolocation inferredSkills field mapped to SkillRegistry via STACK_TO_SKILLS
Error handling for npx skills failures (not installed, network error, skill not found)
